rows.text: resolves dword `[rcx]` through `0020E600`; when the result is non-null it resolves the same dword again and, when byte `+0x6` of that result is non-zero, stores the low word of `edx` to word `+0x60` of `rcx`; on either failed test it returns without writing

resolves dword `[rcx]` through `0020E600` and walks byte `rcx+0x4` entries of `0x30` bytes starting at word `+0x2A` of the result, comparing each word shifted right by 4 with `edx`; it returns the index of the first equal entry, or `0xFFF` when none matches (including a zero count)
stores 0 to byte `+0x0` and word `+0x2` of `rcx` and returns with `eax` 0
when byte `[rcx]` is non-zero, copies dword `+0x10` to `+0x18` and dword `+0x14` to `+0x1C`, stores 0 to byte `+0x0` and the dword `0x3F800000` to `+0xC`; when it is zero it returns without writing
keeps only the low four bits of byte `+0x9` of `rcx` (AND `0xF`) and stores 0 to byte `+0x8`

ANDs byte `+0x9` of `rcx` with `0x3F`; when `edx` is 0 it ORs `0x40` into that byte and stores 0 to byte `+0x8`; otherwise, when the byte has a bit of `0x30` set, it clears `0x20` and sets `0x10` in it and then, if the new byte is below `0x40` and byte `+0x8` is 0, stores qword 8 to `+0x10`, word 1 to `+0xA` and byte 1 to `+0x8` (returning 1); every other case returns with no further write

when byte `+0x8` of `rcx` is non-zero, stores 0 there and the dword `0x3F800000` to `+0x38`, resolves dword `[rcx]` through `0020E600`, and for dword `rcx+0x4` (unsigned count) entries of `0x50` bytes in the result copies each entry's dword `+0x8` to its dword `+0xC`; when the byte is zero it returns without writing
stores 0 to byte `+0xA4` and word `+0xA6` of `rcx` and returns with `eax` 0

ANDs byte `+0x1` of `rcx` with `0xF`; then, when byte `[rcx]` is non-zero, copies dword `+0x10` to `+0x88` and dword `+0x4C` to `+0x8C`, stores 0 to byte `+0x0` and the dword `0x3F800000` to `+0xC`; when it is zero it returns after the AND alone

notes: The `0x3F800000` stores in 00471380, 00515610 and 005175C0 are immediates the listing does not decode as f32; they are written as the raw dword (the IEEE bits of 1.0). 00471B20: the `jae` at 00471B39 compares the byte after the AND `0x3F` and AND `0xDF` OR `0x10`, so it cannot exceed `0x3F`; the branch looks unreachable but is stated as written. 0040DB00 does not test the `0020E600` result for null. 004719A0's AND is its entry instruction; the row anchors only the following store.
